To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of conditioned reinforcement has a significant effect on choice in the absence of concurrent changes in primary reinforcement rate.
the relative rate of S+-producing observing responses is well described by the matching law when the relative rate of primary reinforcement remains constant.

the rate of conditioned reinforcement is a determinant of choice behavior and that the rate of primary reinforcement and the value of the stimulus that serves as a conditioned reinforcer are not independent variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of relative conditioned reinforcement rates on choice.

the development of a behavioral theory of choice and preference that can account for choice between concurrent schedules of reinforcement, concurrent schedules of conditioned reinforcement, concurrent schedules that include a mixture of reinforcement and extinction, and choice between conditioned reinforcers.
the effects of relative rate of primary and conditioned reinforcement on choice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are consistent with the generalized matching law and with the functional similarity of primary and conditioned reinforcer.
the generalized matching law is consistent with the effects of conditioned reinforcement rate on concurrent responding.

these data are not inconsistent with delay reduction and are consistent with general choice models. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2012 APA, all rights reserved)

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of conditioned reinforcement affects choice behavior in a manner similar to the effects of primary reinforcement rate.
the value of a conditioned reinforcer is a function of the value of the reinforcer that it signals and the relative rate of delivery of the signaled reinforcer.
the value of conditioned reinforcement depends on the relative frequency of the conditioned reinforcers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of conditioned reinforcement on choice are similar to the effects of primary reinforcement.
, in addition to matching the rate of primary reinforcement, the rate of conditioned reinforcement is also important in choice.
, in the context of concurrent schedules of reinforcement, conditioned reinforcers are functionally similar to primary reinforcers.
